Forgent Power Solutions.why: Builds the data-center electrical 'powertrain' (switchgear, transformers, eHouses, modular power skids); data centers are its fastest-growing end market, so its revenue scales directly with AI data-center construction.
Forgent Power Solutions.evidence: CEO: 'Revenue growth in the quarter was led by custom products and Powertrain Solutions for data center customers' (CFO); 'We received our first direct order from a frontier AI lab in the fourth quarter, and we have also signed an MSA with a hyperscaler.'

players.product: Data-center electrical distribution equipment (the 'powertrain'): medium/low-voltage switchgear and switchboards, transformers, automatic transfer switches, PDUs, eHouses and prefabricated modular power skids (Powertrain Solutions)

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal Q4 (June quarter) revenue rose 94% year-over-year to a record $462 million (+22% sequentially, all organic), led by custom products and Powertrain Solutions for data center customers. Powertrain Solutions revenue +187% to $147 million; custom products +73% to $292 million; services +69% to $12 million; standard products +3% to $11 million. Adjusted EBITDA +163% to a record $113 million; adjusted EBITDA margin 24.4% (+200 bp sequentially, +640 bp year-over-year, the second consecutive quarter of 200 bp sequential expansion); adjusted net income +275% to $77 million.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 FY2026 revenue $462 million (+94% YoY, +22% QoQ); Powertrain Solutions $147 million (+187%); adjusted EBITDA $113 million (+163%), margin 24.4%

quarterly_data.signal: Full fiscal 2026: revenue +89% to $1.42 billion; adjusted EBITDA +91% to $323 million; adjusted net income +136% to $208 million, each above the high end of the guidance raised in May. By end market, data center revenue grew 161% (customer count +18%, average revenue per customer +121%), which CEO Gary Niederpruem put at roughly four times a market the company estimates grew approximately 37%; grid revenue +69% (customer count +7%, average revenue per customer +58%); industrial and other +11%. Powertrain Solutions rose from 13% of revenue in fiscal 2025 to 25% in fiscal 2026. Operating cash flow increased approximately 2.5x to $109 million from $45 million.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 revenue $1.42 billion (+89%); adjusted EBITDA $323 million (+91%); data center revenue +161%; grid +69%; Powertrain Solutions 25% of revenue (13% in FY2025)

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 bookings reached a record $1.5 billion, +375% year-over-year and +73% sequentially, led by data centers across custom products and Powertrain Solutions; book-to-bill a record 3.3x. Backlog an all-time high $3 billion at year-end, +256% year-over-year and +53% sequentially (versus $850 million entering fiscal 2026), now approximately 40% Powertrain Solutions and more than 2x fiscal 2026 revenue. Records for bookings and backlog for seven consecutive quarters. CEO: backlog is '100% firm commitments and purchase orders' with no LOIs or MOUs; pricing 'remains very consistent'; 'in terms of meaningful push-outs, we are not seeing that for our product set.' Service backlog approximately three times FY2026 service revenue. From fiscal 2027 the company will report orders and backlog only annually, replaced quarterly by next-quarter revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 bookings $1.5 billion (+375% YoY), book-to-bill 3.3x; backlog $3 billion (+256% YoY, +53% QoQ), ~40% Powertrain Solutions

quarterly_data.signal: Fiscal 2027 guidance: revenue $2.4 billion-$2.6 billion (76% growth at the midpoint), adjusted EBITDA $575 million-$625 million (86% growth at the midpoint, implying an adjusted EBITDA margin of approximately 24%, up from 22.7%), adjusted EPS $1.26-$1.40 (approximately 95% growth at the midpoint). Backlog with production slots allocated covers more than 90% of the revenue guidance; the remainder of backlog delivers in fiscal 2028. First-quarter guidance: revenue $445 million-$465 million and adjusted EBITDA $90 million-$100 million (61% revenue and 46% adjusted EBITDA growth at the midpoint), including approximately $10 million of one-time costs; CFO Ryan Fiedler: Q1 EBITDA margin about 21%, then 'a couple of hundred basis points of margin expansion in Q2 from Q1'. Operating cash flow of more than $300 million expected; capital expenditures to step down to roughly 3% of sales (11% in fiscal 2025, 8% in fiscal 2026).
quarterly_data.figure: FY2027 revenue $2.4 billion-$2.6 billion; adjusted EBITDA $575 million-$625 million (~24% margin); adjusted EPS $1.26-$1.40; Q1 revenue $445 million-$465 million; backlog covers more than 90% of FY2027 revenue guidance

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: 'We received our first direct order from a frontier AI lab in the fourth quarter, and we have also signed an MSA with a hyperscaler.' He described the frontier AI lab (not named) as 'pursuing one of the largest AI infrastructure build-outs in the U.S.'; 'this is only the initial award. The customer's first campus alone is expected to exceed one gigawatt, and the broader opportunity for additional orders is measured in multiple gigawatts.' The company's data center route to market has moved from EPCs, engineering firms and OEMs to regional, national and international colocation providers and neo-cloud customers; management sees hyperscalers and frontier AI labs as 'largely untapped' and a significant organic growth opportunity over the next 24 months.
quarterly_data.figure: first direct frontier AI lab order (initial award; first campus expected to exceed one gigawatt); MSA signed with a hyperscaler

quarterly_data.signal: Across fiscal 2025 and 2026 the company invested approximately $190 million to bring more than 1.8 million sq ft of new manufacturing capacity online in all five campuses, expanding the footprint from roughly 480,000 sq ft to 2.3 million sq ft (roughly a five-fold increase); construction is complete or nearing completion and plants are progressing toward target production rates. Manufacturing headcount nearly doubled (roughly 1,800 people at the end of 2025 to around 3,500 and 3,600). CEO: 'we are inside the expected lead times for every product line that we have in the industry'; on supply chain, 'there isn't anything habitual that says this part went from 50 weeks out to 100 weeks.'
quarterly_data.figure: manufacturing footprint 480,000 sq ft to 2.3 million sq ft (~$190 million invested); headcount ~1,800 to ~3,500-3,600; lead times inside market expectations

quarterly_data.signal: Announced an incremental investment to build a dedicated 385,000 sq ft Powertrain Solutions facility at the Tijuana, Mexico campus (roughly 80% the size of its largest plant). Once complete it raises Powertrain Solutions manufacturing capacity by more than 50% to over 1 million sq ft and total revenue capacity to approximately $5.8 billion (an increase of about $800 million); expected online in the fourth quarter of fiscal 2027. CEO: Powertrain Solutions (e-houses, modular skids) 'really seems to be the dominant deployment mechanism for a lot of our customers'; hiring is again being accelerated in Q1 for a significant production ramp.
quarterly_data.figure: 385,000 sq ft Tijuana Powertrain Solutions facility; total revenue capacity ~$5.8 billion; online Q4 FY2027

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on the shift to modular construction: data center customers say modular construction 'can compress portions of the build schedule by roughly 30%-50%'; modular and prefabricated construction is approximately 40% of data center construction today versus 10%-20% in the cloud era. Customers increasingly want to move work from the field to the factory to reduce reliance on field labor and accelerate speed to power, which expands Forgent's addressable wallet. Vertical integration back to sheet metal fabrication and facilities near every major U.S. data center hub cited as advantages; an e-house can be approximately 60 ft long and weigh as much as 50 tons. Powertrain Solutions margins are 'within a standard deviation' of point products, except where third-party gear in a solution carries a lower markup.
quarterly_data.figure: modular ~40% of data center construction today; build schedule compressed by roughly 30%-50% (customer feedback)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on demand: 'Our conversations with customers indicate that capital spending plans are being revised upward from where they were even just six months ago'; 'we are not hearing anything about any massive projects being delayed or the market slowing.' Existing customers from a year or two ago are 'spending anywhere from 30%-100% more with us' as Forgent sells multiple product lines and integrated solutions. The company is in discussions with several customers about longer-term commitments. Fiscal 2027 guidance midpoint is around 30% above the December 2025 IPO forecast ($2.5 billion versus $1.8 billion revenue; $600 million versus $469 million adjusted EBITDA) and matches the IPO model's fiscal 2028 revenue. M&A is the first capital-allocation priority as free cash flow builds (product line extensions, services, possible geographic expansion).
quarterly_data.figure: existing customers spending 30%-100% more; FY2027 guidance midpoint around 30% above IPO forecast
